claims.text: The proposed intervention is to use machine learning and molecular dynamics simulations.
Current experimental and computational methods have limited accuracy for determining the specified melting and liquid-state properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Current experimental and computational methods provide limited availability of the specified thermodynamic data.
Current experimental and computational methods are inefficient across large high-entropy-alloy composition spaces.
Configurational entropy affects solid-solution phase formation in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Mixing enthalpy is relevant to solid-solution phase formation in multicomponent alloys.
Gibbs free energy is a mediator connecting the proposed computational methods to solid-solution phase formation.

Machine learning and molecular dynamics can accurately predict melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Accounting for configurational entropy, mixing enthalpy, and Gibbs free energy is sufficient to produce accurate predictions of the specified melting and liquid-state properties.
The intervention will improve predictive accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the availability of melting and liquid-state thermodynamic data.
The intervention will improve efficiency relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The predicted improvements apply across a large compositional space of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The predicted improvements apply to both high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Significant deviation between predicted properties and experimental data would falsify the hypothesis.
